top30.title: Agentic profiles for effective AI governance
top30.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10805-zA framework comprising four dimensions—autonomy, efficacy, goal complexity and generality—is proposed for characterizing AI agents, supporting the construction of agentic profiles for the effective governance of different AI agents.

top30.title: Beyond representational alignment with brain-guided language models for robust reasoning
top30.abstract: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 03 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01278-wXiao et al. show that large language models partially align with human brain activity during deductive reasoning. They further show that brain signals can directly guide and improve model performance, with transfer across reasoning types.

top30.title: Towards principled knowledge editing methods for large language model reasoning
top30.abstract: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01276-yChen et al. explore limitations of current knowledge editing techniques in large language models and propose three promising research directions that respect the complexity of knowledge representation in a real-world setting.

top30.title: No single rule explains how climate affects carbon storage in tropical forests

top30.title: Trajectory forecasting lifts the femtosecond ceiling in molecular simulation
top30.abstract: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 05 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01275-zA new deep learning method enables molecular dynamics simulations over longer time scales while still achieving accurate physical property prediction.

top30.title: Disruption of the research software landscape through AI software generation
top30.abstract: Nature Methods, Published online: 17 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03210-xSpecialized research software has historically been costly and time-consuming to create, but large language models (LLMs) have become capable enough at code generation to fundamentally change this. We describe how LLM-assisted programming disrupts the landscape by allowing researchers to build tools without support from software engineers, illustrate this with an example built rapidly by a single LLM-assisted developer, and discuss opportunities and risks.

top30.title: An explainable biomedical foundation model via large-scale concept-enhanced vision–language pretraining
top30.abstract: Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 17 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01764-xConceptCLIP is an explainable foundation model that leverages MedConcept-23M, a large-scale dataset comprising 23 million biomedical image–text–concept triplets, for precise and interpretable medical image analysis and diagnostics.

top30.title: Foundation models in biomedical imaging: turning hype into reality
top30.abstract: Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01762-zThis Perspective assesses the role of foundation models as clinical tools and introduces real-world evaluation and assessment of foundation models (REAL-FM), a framework for assessing data, technical readiness and clinical value towards responsible artificial intelligence.

top30.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10724-zShocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula, detected in Hα emission with the MOTHRA telescope, provide evidence for the recycling of fragmented stellar ejecta into the surrounding gas.

top30.title: Evidence for the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way
top30.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10878-wDeep Hubble Space Telescope imaging of the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC 9050-Dw1 reveals an extragalactic globular cluster stream, with analysis and modelling probing the rich dark matter content of the host galaxy.

top30.title: Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass
top30.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10880-2An analysis of the relationships between aboveground biomass and various climatic factors in three major regions of tropical forest shows that understanding the complex interactions between climate, topography and soils is crucial to predict how climate change will affect carbon storage capacity.

top30.title: Bow shocks reveal how a dying star returns matter to interstellar space
top30.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02159-3Deep imaging of ionized gas in the Helix Nebula uncovers many curved shock waves around a dying Sun-like star. These ‘bow shocks’ are produced when ejected shells of stellar material break up and race outwards. Their changing shapes imply that the shell fragments are being stripped, shredded and mixed into interstellar gas over roughly 10,000 years.
